verdict.rationale: A business-operations SaaS could plausibly let users configure their own background automations, so the axis applies. The evidence only describes vendor-run, built-in services: automatic book reconciliation, automated sales-tax filings and payments, nexus monitoring, and annual reports filed on the user's behalf. These are adjacent managed features, not automations the user sets up, and nothing documents user-defined triggers, workflows or scheduled jobs.
